ARM: ref 1dee9e25f6, XEMU_OPT_FIFO_SKEW_BOUND default 0 (pfifo.c:95), Galleon (USA).xiso.iso, 240 s, THOR, two runs queued separately under one --who because the replicate for a no-oracle measurement is the RUN and not the window.

G1 -- THE IMPOSSIBLE ROW. Xd == 0 on both runs. A bit cannot go from set to clear between two back-to-back scans with nothing between them but the probe's own arithmetic. Non-zero indicts the instrument and voids every leg below. Fails in a real world: wrong page arithmetic at a DIRTY_MEMORY_BLOCK_SIZE boundary, an unstable RCU pointer, or the pfifo and render threads overlapping where this assumes they do not.

G2 -- THE DENOMINATORS ARE LIVE, and this is the leg that stops a zero being read as an absence. Per run: vtx_copies > 50,000 AND tex_uploads > 5,000 AND tex_windows > 100,000. A thin tex_uploads is the documented tell for a mis-placed window -- ref ae0283fe2d gave 950 of 487,013 and reported a rate of zero over it, which reads exactly like G3's decisive outcome. If G2 fails on a run, G3/G4/G5 are NOT MEASURED on that run rather than zero.

G3 -- THE TEXTURE SITE, AN ABSOLUTE. Tr/tex_uploads <= 1.0e-03 on each run, and the reported figure is Tr with its 3/N one-sided 95% bound, never a bare zero. Predicted Tr == 0, bound <= about 1.3e-04 per upload pooled. The world in which this FAILS and it is not far-fetched: the tip is ~300 commits past 5cfc236d9b, Galleon's texture-upload count could rise the way Crimson's rose 53% across a comparable span, and a title that starts rewriting bound textures every frame races the way Crimson does at 0.57-0.62. Nothing in this survey forces the number.

G4 -- THE VERTEX SITE FIRES, AN ABSOLUTE. Vr > 0 pooled over the two runs, and 1.0e-05 <= Vr/vtx_copies <= 1.0e-03 pooled. Predicted about 6.3e-05. Registered as a pooled rate with a bracket rather than a per-run count because the nova runs gave 12, 8 and 5 -- Poisson counts whose per-run spread is 2.2x and means nothing, while the pooled rate is the quantity. Fails if the Thor's timing or the tip's 300 commits put it outside the bracket, which is exactly the finding that would be worth having.

G5 -- THE INVERSION, and it is the one leg here that contradicts a registered prediction rather than replicating a number. #54 v3's leg 4 predicted Vr/vtx_copies < Tr/tex_uploads on the reasoning that the texture window is orders of magnitude longer than the vertex memcpy. On GALLEON that ordering is INVERTED in the nova data. Predicted here: Vr/vtx_copies > Tr/tex_uploads on Galleon at this ref on the Thor. The mechanism is not window length, it is EXPOSURE: a race needs the guest to be rewriting the buffer, and Galleon rewrites vertex arrays constantly (about 550 dirty vertex copies per second) while barely rewriting bound textures. v3's leg 4 named this failing world in advance -- "a title streaming dynamic vertex buffers rewrites them immediately before drawing from them far more often than it rewrites textures, which inverts the ordering" -- and Galleon is that title.

G6 -- THE EXPOSURE RATIO, which is what makes G3's zero an explanation instead of a mystery. tex_uploads/tex_windows <= 5.0e-02 on each run. Predicted about 1.4e-02, against Crimson Skies' 0.75-0.80 on the same instrument -- a 60x difference in how often a draw's texture read follows an unsynced guest write. This is the quantity that says Galleon's Tr == 0 is a statement about Galleon's WORKLOAD and not about the emulator's memory ordering, and it is the reason the barrier arm's zero and this zero are not the same zero.

Tq is REPORTED and carries no verdict -- it is a per-window query count and its median moved 201 -> 234 between the nova's mode-0 and mode-2 arms, so it tracks the configuration and not the probe.

ASSERTIONS, recorded so they are not counted as falsifiers because the code forces them: Tr <= tex_uploads <= tex_windows, and Vr <= vtx_copies.

WHAT THIS SURVEY CANNOT SEE, written before the run.
 (1) #44's `cut == complete` case. If the guest COMPLETES the successor write before the poll's test-and-clear consumes the bits, the upload reads a fully written successor and nothing is set again. Tr is a FLOOR on version skew and a CEILING on byte-level overlap (4 KiB pages), and those are different quantities; neither is "the rate at which frames are corrupted".
 (2) Whether any counted race corrupted a frame. A soak writes no captures. This is #54's standing exclusion and this survey does not lift it.
 (3) The surface-upload read, deliberately uninstrumented: nothing on the device clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a surface range, so the bitmap is monotone there and a probe on it would print a plausible number with no time base in it.
 (4) #79's vertex skew, IF that suite's vertices do not pass sync_vertex_ram_buffer. That is a denominator question and it is being answered by a SEPARATE Stencil-disc request under the same --who rather than assumed here; the 4-suite discs carrying Stencil read vtx_copies = 34 per run against ~46,000 draw windows, which is either "Stencil owns most of those 34 and the counter is merely underpowered" or "Stencil owns none of them and the counter is structurally blind to #79". A zero from a blind instrument is not evidence, which is the whole reason that request exists.
 (5) Whether Galleon's vertex races are #79's mechanism at all. Same site and same shape, different workload; this survey measures a rate, not an attribution.

FORM. ab_compare's machine-readable slots are per-capture and a soak produces no captures, so expect_counts are degenerate on purpose: better=0, worse=0, must_not_move '*'. If ANY capture appears, the request was mis-dispatched as a suites run and every leg is void. The legs are numbers read off the hakuX-perf line by docs/testing/vram_race_report.py, and they are bound here by this file's content hash -- which matters MORE for a soak than for a disc arm, not less, because nothing computes a verdict and every reading is interpreted by hand. The hash is what makes a leg quietly widened once the numbers arrive detectable.
